title: Ford and GM OBD-I interpretation
learningObjective: Resolve manufacturer-dependent numeric code meanings and retrieval context

equipment.label: Legacy code evidence input (developmental stand-in)
equipment.notes: Minimal original stand-in authored for this lab. It supplies illustrative flash-code observations and a written retrieval procedure. It contains no manufacturer code table, no reproduced glossary and no OEM definition, and it is not a completed reference tool.

equipment.label: Vehicle profile input (developmental stand-in)
equipment.notes: Minimal original stand-in that supplies the make/year/engine/test-mode context OBD-I interpretation requires. The profile is explicitly illustrative training context, not a real vehicle identity and not a source of code meaning. It is not a completed tool and provides no lookup capability.

points: Do not connect or disconnect anything on a simulated live circuit; describe the step instead.
Confirm the retrieval method and test mode before interpreting any code, because meaning depends on them.
Treat every code as an observation from a monitored condition until supporting evidence exists.
State clearly when a code meaning cannot be established from the information available.
safetyBriefing.boundaries: Simulated and paper-based only. No physical retrieval is performed. No manufacturer code definition, numeric threshold or service procedure is provided, asserted or implied, because no verified source is available to this project.

instructorDemonstration.summary: Demonstrate why the same numeric code can mean different things across manufacturers and test modes, and how to record an interpretation that is honest about what cannot be established.
steps: Read the illustrative vehicle profile and state which context items constrain interpretation.
Show two illustrative retrieval procedures and explain how the test mode changes what a code means.
Demonstrate recording an observation without asserting a definition that no verified source supports.
Show how to mark an unresolved code meaning as requiring a verified source rather than guessing.

scenario.symptom: Illustrative legacy vehicle with a stored condition reported during a self-test. Flash-code observations are supplied; the code meanings are not, because no verified source is available to this project.
scenario.systemContext: OBD-I interpretation depends on manufacturer, model year, engine, retrieval method and test mode. Students must establish that context before interpreting anything, then record what remains unresolved.

vehicleContext.make: Illustrative legacy manufacturer A (training label, not a real vehicle identity)
vehicleContext.testMode: Illustrative key-on-engine-off self-test with flash-code output

measurements.label: Illustrative flash-code observation (training value)
measurements.conditions: illustrative key-on-engine-off self-test, warm ambient, no load applied
measurements.limitations: Authored for practice. This is not a real retrieval result, and the numeric value has no asserted meaning here. Meaning requires a verified manufacturer source and the full context above.

measurements.label: Retrieval context recorded alongside the observation
measurements.value: make, model year, engine and test mode recorded as supplied
measurements.conditions: recorded before interpretation, per the supplied procedure
measurements.limitations: Context values are illustrative training labels. They are not verified vehicle data.

descriptors: No waveform is supplied in Week 3 and no scope work is expected.
Students state whether an electrical measurement would add useful evidence to a code interpretation, and why.
waveformEvidence.notes: No sampled trace is supplied and none is implied.

scenario.uncertainty: Code meaning is unresolved in this lab by design. Students must record the code as an observation, state the context that would be required to interpret it, and state that a verified source is needed. No manufacturer definition may be asserted.

competingHypotheses.statement: The stored condition reflects a genuine circuit or component fault that further electrical testing would isolate.
evidenceFor: The self-test reported a stored condition during the stated test mode.
evidenceAgainst: A stored condition indicates a monitored condition was detected; it does not identify which component caused it, and the code meaning is unresolved here.

competingHypotheses.statement: The stored condition was set by a condition that is no longer present, or by a retrieval performed in the wrong test mode.
evidenceFor: Test mode and retrieval method change what a code means, and the procedure must be confirmed before interpretation.
evidenceAgainst: No re-test or clearing-and-retest evidence has been supplied, so persistence has not been established.

testSelectionOptions.label: Confirm make, year, engine and test mode before attempting any interpretation
testSelectionOptions.justificationPrompt: Explain why the same numeric code cannot be interpreted without this context, and what could go wrong if it were assumed.
testSelectionOptions.expectedObservation: A recorded context statement, with any unavailable item explicitly marked unknown.

testSelectionOptions.label: Record the code as an observation and mark the meaning as requiring a verified source
testSelectionOptions.justificationPrompt: Explain the difference between recording an observation and asserting a definition, and why the distinction matters.
testSelectionOptions.expectedObservation: An observation record that contains no asserted manufacturer meaning.

testSelectionOptions.label: Propose an electrical test that would add evidence without needing the code definition
testSelectionOptions.justificationPrompt: Explain what the test would establish and what result would change your thinking, without relying on an unresolved code meaning.
testSelectionOptions.expectedObservation: A test that gathers independent evidence about the circuit rather than restating the code.

prompts: Record the retrieval context: make, model year, engine, retrieval method and test mode, marking anything unknown.
Record the flash-code observation exactly as supplied, without adding a meaning.
State which information would be required to interpret the code, and why the project cannot assert it now.
Propose one independent electrical test and state what it would establish.
State how you would distinguish a currently present condition from a stored one that is no longer active.

steps: Re-state the retrieval context and confirm the observation was taken under the same conditions.
Confirm the interpretation section contains no asserted manufacturer meaning.
State what evidence would be required before any repair is claimed as verified.
expectedEvidence: A record that separates the raw observation from any interpretation.
An explicit statement that a verified source and a re-test are both required before a repair is claimed as verified.

accessibility.keyboardPath: Tab from the skip link to the vehicle-profile panel and the legacy-code evidence panel, then through hypothesis cards, test buttons and worksheet fields.
textAlternatives: Flash-code observations are presented as text, not as an animated lamp sequence, so no information depends on timing or motion.
All context, hypothesis and evidence content is text and is reachable in document order.
notes: No canvas or animated element is used in this lab.
Selection and status feedback is announced through a polite live region.
Long context values wrap rather than requiring horizontal scrolling.

technicalReviewChecklist.statement: No manufacturer code definition, OEM threshold or service procedure is asserted anywhere in this lab.
Retrieval context (make, year, engine, test mode) is required before interpretation.
The code is treated as an observation of a monitored condition, not proof of a failed component.
Stand-ins are described as limited developmental inputs, not completed reference tools.
Instructor material is stored outside the student tree and is not reachable from this page.
